gen-dafont-brusher-fs-synonym: Synonym lays down a plain stripe of constant ink with generous openings in every curve. Brusher is the showy one, a calligraphic script whose curves are as heavy as its stems, while Synonym keeps things dependable and clean.
gen-dafont-brusher-plus-jakarta-sans: Romantic, brushed energy up top, all calligraphic sweep and heavy curves. And Plus Jakarta Sans follows in a monoline plain sans, its curve endings kept well apart, so the heading would feel lost if made small.
gen-dafont-burnstown-dam-fs-karma: Karma is a trustworthy serif whose terminals finish well clear of the stem, with only a mild modulation, while Burnstown Dam stays closed and geometric above it. Expect it to read smoothly, never snagging the eye.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-abeezee: Neon-tube lines, spaced far apart. Bushcraft keeps one thickness through every curve, and ABeeZee underneath is a plain sans with open terminals and a high mean line, so the two sit together without competing.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-aldrich: Expressive Bushcraft spaces its letters extra wide, with capitals barely rising above the lowercase and closed shapes throughout. Aldrich is a plain sans with a tall x-height and cupped round letters, so the text feels like tracing one thick thread.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-anek-bangla: Wide-set, glowing letters. Bushcraft is best at that single neon-tube track with closed shapes, while Anek Bangla does its work in open, wide s curves and a short rise from midline to ascender.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-anek-gujarati: Bushcraft spaces its closed, uniform letters extra wide, with no thick-thin flicker, while Anek Gujarati opens up beneath it with a gaping c. That openness against the closed heading is the whole story.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-anek-latin: Artistic Bushcraft spaces its closed, thin-looking letters extra wide, with capitals barely standing out. Anek Latin answers in a plain sans whose tall lowercase nearly reaches the capitals, held open rather than curled shut.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-comme: Comme reads smoothly, with no clogged curves and lowercase bodies filling most of the letter height. Bushcraft above it keeps its line width through every turn, wide-spaced and a bit showy, and the text feels easy going beneath.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-cossette-texte: Bushcraft spaces its closed, uniform letters extra wide, with capitals barely rising above the lowercase. Cossette Texte is a plain sans with wide-eyed e shapes and a prominent x-height, so shrinking the heading would let it nearly vanish.
